plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Cell Membrane Architecture & Permeability chart from Overton (1895 Vierteljahrsschr. Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 40: 159–201), Gorter & Grendel (1 April 1925 J. Exp. Med. 41: 439–443), Skou (February 1957 Biochim. Biophys. teach_overlay.detail: Inked phospholipid bilayer & membrane transport chart on period paper showing Gorter & Grendel's 2.0:1 lipid monolayer-to-erythrocyte area ratio (5 nm bilayer thickness), Skou's Na+/K+-ATPase pump (3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in per ATP, consuming ~30% of resting mammalian ATP), and Agre's Aquaporin-1 water channel (~3,000,000,000 H2O molecules/second with 0 proton leakage)
teach_overlay.scale: the membrane around every cell in your body is a self-sealing soap bubble just two molecules thick — twenty thousand times thinner than a sheet of kitchen paper, yet studded with protein gates that check the passport of every atom trying to cross
